facts.fact: The Ministry of Health's report for 2024 says its Department of Policy, Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation is responsible for registering and certifying births and deaths, through a Birth and Death Registration unit under the Bureau of Vital Statistics, and that the Ministry set up the DHIS2 birth registration platform through its partners.

The Ministry of Health reports among its 2024 achievements that it developed a National Birth and Death Registration Policy to improve services and set guidelines for registration and certification; the report does not say whether the policy names the DHIS2 platform.

The Ministry of Health says birth registration was decentralised with help from partners (UNICEF, World Bank and others) and the DHIS2 platform set up through its partners, while budgetary constraint inhibits the Ministry's ability to sustain the birth registration centres and to absorb their staff on payroll; no domestic budget line is stated.
The Ministry of Health's report for 2024 says birth and death registration have been integrated into the DHIS2 platform, to improve monitoring and reporting of both.
The Ministry of Health states that as of 2023, 93,031 birth registrations had been recorded in DHIS2, which it gives as 67 per cent of all birth registrations and certifications.

The Ministry of Health's report for 2024 describes a web-based birth registration platform on DHIS2 on which county birth registration teams register and certify births online, with GSM scratch cards supplied for the connection, and petrol supplied to collect application forms from health facilities and return certificates to them.

The Ministry of Health says that six years before its 2024 report the country processed and issued birth certificates on an offline, non-centralised information management system, since replaced by the DHIS2 platform.
facts.system: offline, non-centralised information management system for birth certificates

facts.fact: The Ministry of Health says birth registration centres have been established in all 15 counties since 2010 and that the service is decentralised to all counties for children aged 0-12, but gives no count of centres or of those entering births on the web platform.

In 2024 the Ministry of Health trained over 45 national and county birth registration personnel on the web-based platform, procured 35 antivirus licences for county birth registration computers that had been breaking down, and developed a National Birth and Death Registration Policy.
